receiver.requested_changes:
1) Reduce purchase price from USD 45,000,000 to USD 40,000,000 (or, at minimum, include an earn-out / purchase price adjustment tied to working capital and net debt).
2) Extend closing to at least 75-90 days after signing, and make closing conditional on completion of all customary due diligence and Buyer-satisfactory deliverables.
3) Expand Seller representations to be full, not just knowledge-qualified, and cover title to shares, authority, no conflicts, compliance with law, no undisclosed liabilities, accuracy of financial statements, and absence of material adverse changes.
4) Add customary indemnity protections, a cap basket structure favorable to Buyer, and survival periods consistent with a meaningful recourse package.
5) Clarify confidentiality so it is mutual and subject to customary disclosure exceptions.
receiver.message_back:
Dear colleagues,

Thank you for sending over the draft. We appreciate the clean starting point.

From our side, the current draft is not yet workable on economics or risk allocation. In particular, the purchase price is too high for a starting point, the closing timetable is too compressed, and the seller protections are too narrow.

Our initial comments are as follows:

- Price: USD 45,000,000 is above where our client can proceed. We propose USD 40,000,000, or alternatively a structure that includes a post-closing adjustment and/or earn-out tied to working capital and net debt.
- Closing: 45 days is too short. We would want 75-90 days from signing, with closing subject to completion of customary diligence and delivery of all Buyer-satisfactory closing deliverables.
- Reps: The seller’s representations should not be limited to knowledge and should extend beyond the financial statements. We need the usual full suite of seller reps, including title, authority, no conflicts, compliance, no undisclosed liabilities, and no material adverse change.
- Protection: We will also need customary indemnity provisions, survival periods, and liability mechanics that provide meaningful recourse for the Buyer.
- Confidentiality: Please make this mutual and subject to standard permitted disclosures.

Please send a revised draft reflecting the above, and we can turn comments quickly.

Best,
Bellweather Croft LLP

drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Dear colleagues,

Thank you for the thoughtful comments. We have revised the draft to reflect a number of market-standard points and to advance the discussion.

We have not moved on headline value, which remains an important point for our client, but we have expanded the seller covenant package and added a customary indemnity framework so that the agreement is closer to executable form.

As you will see, we have also made confidentiality mutual and incorporated standard permitted disclosure exceptions. On timing, we have adjusted the closing mechanics modestly, while keeping the process efficient and tied to customary deliverables.

We have not adopted a buyer-satisfaction standard for diligence or deliverables, nor a broader earn-out / purchase-price re-trade structure at this stage, but we are happy to continue working through your mark-up to narrow the remaining issues quickly.

Best,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 2. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 for the Shares, subject only to any mutually agreed, customary post-closing adjustment mechanism expressly set out in this Agreement.

3. Closing. Closing shall occur within 60 days of signing, subject to completion of customary closing deliverables reasonably required to effect the transaction in substantially the form contemplated by this Agreement.

4. Representations. The Seller represents that: (a) the Seller has the requisite authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (b) the Seller holds good title to the Shares and will transfer such title free and clear of liens and encumbrances; (c) this Agreement does not conflict with any material agreement or obligation binding on the Seller; (d) the Seller has complied in all material respects with applicable law in connection with the ownership and transfer of the Shares; (e) there are no undisclosed liabilities of the Company other than liabilities incurred in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice; (f) the financial statements fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition of the Company; and (g) there has been no material adverse change in the business of the Company since the date of the latest financial statements.

5. Indemnity. The Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for direct losses arising from a breach of the Seller’s representations or covenants in this Agreement, subject to: (i) a basket of USD 250,000 on a deductible basis; (ii) an aggregate cap equal to 10% of the Purchase Price, except in the case of fraud or willful misconduct; and (iii) survival periods of 12 months for general claims, 18 months for tax matters, and the applicable statute of limitations for fraud or fundamental title/authority claims.

6. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement are confidential, and each party may disclose such terms only to its representatives, financing sources, insurers, and advisers, and as otherwise required by law or stock exchange rule, in each case subject to customary confidentiality obligations where applicable.

receiver.requested_changes: 1) Reduce the purchase price from USD 45,000,000 or, at minimum, add a buyer-favorable net debt/working capital adjustment and an escrow/holdback. 2) Replace the open-ended “customary closing deliverables” standard with a finite list of objective, seller-deliverable conditions precedent, with failure to satisfy them giving Buyer a walk-away right. 3) Expand the seller’s representations beyond title/authority/basic financials to include corporate power, capitalization, undisclosed liabilities, compliance, litigation, taxes, IP, contracts, employees, and accuracy of disclosures. 4) Add a robust indemnity package for breach of reps, taxes, title, and pre-closing liabilities, with survival periods and a meaningful escrow or cap/basket framework. 5) Make the post-closing adjustment mechanism mandatory, formula-based, and buyer-protective if any adjustment remains. 6) Tighten confidentiality so Buyer can disclose to affiliates, actual/potential financing sources, and professional advisers on a need-to-know basis without unnecessary restrictions, and permit broader disclosure for regulatory and legal compliance.
receiver.message_back:
Dear colleagues,

Thank you for the revised draft. We appreciate the movement on the rep package and confidentiality language.

That said, our client cannot accept the agreement in its current form. The headline price remains too high, and the closing mechanics still leave too much discretion and uncertainty on the Buyer side. To move this toward signature, we need the next draft to reflect the following:

- a reduced purchase price, or at minimum a formulaic, buyer-protective net debt / working capital adjustment with appropriate escrow or holdback;
- objective, finite closing conditions rather than open-ended “customary deliverables” language;
- a fuller seller rep package and a meaningful indemnity regime for breach, taxes, title, and pre-closing liabilities; and
- a more practical confidentiality carve-out for affiliates, lenders, advisers, and regulatory disclosures.

If helpful, we can circulate a clean mark-up focused on these points and get the remaining issues narrowed quickly.

Best,
Bellweather Croft LLP
